title: GitOps Deployment Lead Time
exclusions: Covers the detection logic documented for 'GitOps Deployment Lead Time' only. Does not supplant cross-domain SIEM playbooks for unrelated domains or regulatory attestation. Entities listed in `operational_exceptions.csv` during approved tests are excluded.
evidence: Saved search `operations_gitops_deployment_lead_time` (UC-12.5.10), SOC dashboard panel "Operations — GitOps Deployment Lead Time", and weekly export to `index=audit_evidence` sourcetype=csv:ops_controls.

controlTest.positiveScenario: Ingest synthetic events into `index=devops` sourcetype='github:webhook' that satisfy the UC-12.5.10 SPL filters for 'GitOps Deployment Lead Time'. Run the saved search and confirm at least one alertable row with expected fields populated.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Ingest benign `devops` / `github:webhook` events outside the detection threshold, or exclude the test entity via `ops_exception_register.csv` with a valid window. Confirm zero alert rows for UC-12.5.10.

dataSources: `sourcetype=github:webhook`, `sourcetype=argocd:application` Collected via Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617) modular input or scripted poll into the index named in the SPL.
app: Git + ArgoCD/Flux correlation (custom), DORA metrics scripts — Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617)
spl:
index=devops (sourcetype="github:webhook" OR sourcetype="argocd:application")
| eval commit_ts=if(sourcetype="github:webhook", strptime(commit_time,"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ"), null())
| eval sync_ts=if(sourcetype="argocd:application", _time, null())
| stats earliest(commit_ts) as first_commit, latest(sync_ts) as last_sync by repository, revision
| eval lead_time_sec=last_sync-first_commit
| where isnotnull(lead_time_sec) AND lead_time_sec > 0
| eval lead_time_min=round(lead_time_sec/60,1)
| table repository, revision, lead_time_min
| sort -lead_time_min
description: Measuring Git commit-to-production lead time exposes bottlenecks in review, CI, and sync so teams can optimize end-to-end delivery speed.
value: Early 'GitOps Deployment Lead Time' detection reduces operational risk and delayed incident response by giving Operations operators a Splunk-native signal before manual triage or audit channels surface the issue.
implementation: Correlate Git merge or push timestamps with Argo CD successful sync or Flux `LastAppliedRevision` time for the same revision. Use lookup or transaction across indexes if needed. Report p50/p95 lead time by team and service. Exclude hotfix channels with tags if required.
visualization: Histogram (lead time distribution), Line chart (p95 lead time trend), Bar chart (lead time by service).
knownFalsePositives:
1. **Scheduled maintenance** — Planned change generates expected deviations for 'GitOps Deployment Lead Time'. Cross-check change records.

2. **Batch job cycle** — Fixed-schedule workload skews `devops` metrics.

3. **Monitoring synthetic checks** — Health probes from known hosts.

4. **Onboarding burst** — New entities produce atypical volume until baseline stabilizes.

**Suppression mechanism:** `ops_exception_register.csv` with entity, reason, valid_until.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Install and configure the required add-on or app: Git + ArgoCD/Flux correlation (custom), DORA metrics scripts.
• Ensure the following data sources are available: `sourcetype=github:webhook`, `sourcetype=argocd:application`.
• For app installation, inputs.conf, and Splunk directory layout, see the Implementation guide: docs/implementation-guide.md

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Correlate Git merge or push timestamps with Argo CD successful sync or Flux `LastAppliedRevision` time for the same revision. Use lookup or transaction across indexes if needed. Report p50/p95 lead time by team and service. Exclude hotfix channels with tags if required.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
Run the following SPL in Search (then save as report or alert; adjust time range and threshold as needed):

```spl
index=devops (sourcetype="github:webhook" OR sourcetype="argocd:application")
| eval commit_ts=if(sourcetype="github:webhook", strptime(commit_time,"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ"), null())
| eval sync_ts=if(sourcetype="argocd:application", _time, null())
| stats earliest(commit_ts) as first_commit, latest(sync_ts) as last_sync by repository, revision
| eval lead_time_sec=last_sync-first_commit
| where isnotnull(lead_time_sec) AND lead_time_sec > 0
| eval lead_time_min=round(lead_time_sec/60,1)
| table repository, revision, lead_time_min
| sort -lead_time_min
```

Understanding this SPL

**GitOps Deployment Lead Time** — Measuring Git commit-to-production lead time exposes bottlenecks in review, CI, and sync so teams can optimize end-to-end delivery speed.

Documented **Data sources**: `sourcetype=github:webhook`, `sourcetype=argocd:application`. **App/TA** (typical add-on context): Git + ArgoCD/Flux correlation (custom), DORA metrics scripts. The SPL below should target the same indexes and sourcetypes you configured for that feed—rename `index=` / `sourcetype=` if your deployment differs.

The first pipeline stage scopes events using **index**: devops; **sourcetype**: github:webhook, argocd:application. Those sourcetypes align with what this use case lists under Data sources.

**Pipeline walkthrough**

• Scopes the data: index=devops, sourcetype="github:webhook". Cross-check against **Data sources** above so indexes and sourcetypes match your ingestion.
• `eval` defines or adjusts **commit_ts** — often to normalize units, derive a ratio, or prepare for thresholds.
• `eval` defines or adjusts **sync_ts** — often to normalize units, derive a ratio, or prepare for thresholds.
• `stats` rolls up events into metrics; results are split **by repository, revision** so each row reflects one combination of those dimensions.
• `eval` defines or adjusts **lead_time_sec** — often to normalize units, derive a ratio, or prepare for thresholds.
• Filters the current rows with `where isnotnull(lead_time_sec) AND lead_time_sec > 0` — typically the threshold or rule expression for this monitoring goal.
• `eval` defines or adjusts **lead_time_min** — often to normalize units, derive a ratio, or prepare for thresholds.
• Pipeline stage (see **GitOps Deployment Lead Time**): table repository, revision, lead_time_min
• Orders rows with `sort` — combine with `head`/`tail` for top-N patterns.


Step 3 — Validate
Confirm that events are present in the index and that the search returns expected results. Compare with the GitHub audit log. Verify field extractions and index permissions.


Step 4 — Operationalize
Add the search to a dashboard or set up alert actions (email, webhook, PagerDuty, etc.) as required. Document the use case in your runbook and assign an owner. Consider visualizations: Histogram (lead time distribution), Line chart (p95 lead time trend), Bar chart (lead time by service).
